newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian c.bank says it cannot contain crisis.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian c.bank says it cannot contain crisis.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) on Friday warned it lacked the resources to control the country's deepening economic crisis and urged politicians to resolve a deadlock blocking the formation of a new government.

"The BNB is firmly convinced that if an appropriate solution to the current political crisis is not found...the BNB alone will not be able to contain further depreciation of the national currency, galloping inflation and deepening destabilisation of the financial system," a bank statement said.

Both the opposition and ruling ex-communists see the implementation of a strict monetary regime proposed by the IMF as the solution to the crisis but disagree on what kind of government should manage it.
The Socialists, blamed for causing the economic crisis by delaying reform, have offered elections in December, a year ahead of schedule.
In the meantime they want to form a new cabinet to take over from Socialist prime minister Zhan Videnov, who resigned on December 21. The UDF wants immediate elections in March.
The lev, which has been in freefall as the crisis has worsened, hit a new historic low on Friday of 915 to the dollar on the interbank market from 600 at the beginning of January.
The central bank fixing for Friday was 731.71, compared to 495.74 at the beginning of the year.
Dozens of shops in Sofia have closed down as shopkeepers fear to stock up on goods whose prices change within hours, while impoverished consumers are buying only basic foods.
"There are clear symptoms of hyper-inflation," said National Statistics Institute (NSI) director Zahari Karamfilov.
Inflation for the first 15 days of January alone ran to 30.8 percent, the NSI said. Economists expect this month's inflation to reach 50 percent.
"If monthly inflation is around 35 percent, annual inflation will top 3,600 percent," said Ivan Angelov of the Economy Institute at the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences.

The central bank has exhausted its arsenal of monetary instruments to support the lev. Foreign exchange reserves stood at $518 million in December and are expected fall lower in January after a $135.1 million foreign debt payment. Cash must also be found for vital imports like fuel and grain.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) last year proposed the implementation of a currency board system which severely curbs the financial powers of the government and the central bank.

The opposition says that if early elections were held in March, the new parliament would adopt the legal amendments needed for the implementation of a currency board in April and enable its introduction in May.
The BNB urged politicians to focus efforts on an anti-crisis programme which would speed up structural reform and resume talks with multilateral lenders.
"Any further delay in taking a political decision will lay an enormous burden on the whole nation and further social and economic distress becomes inevitable," the BNB said.

On Friday both the Socialists and opposition showed no signs of compromise in their first round of negotioans brokered by the new President Petar Stoyanov, who was elected on the opposition ticket last year.
